newsitem.title: UK: Prism rejects pressure group report.
newsitem.headline: Prism rejects pressure group report.

text.p: British railway operator Prism Rail Plc said on Monday that it "totally refutes" the conclusions of a report by pressure group Save Our Railways (SOR).
"We are extremely angry that Save Our Railways have chosen to publish this report without any apparent attempt to consult with franchisees," said Giles Fearnley, chief executive of Prism.
The report by SOR said five out of the total 25 train operating companies, including three run by Prism, would make losses whatever assumptions were used.
SOR used four different assumptions, depending on likely increases in net revenue over the next seven years, as the basis for the study.

Prism said that while the report recognises that the railways have suffered through lack of investment prior to privatisation, it "takes no account of the revenue generating investment opportunities that are inherent in our own franchise plans".
It also said that there are other factors that should contribute significantly to revenue growth and that the report fails to reflect its investment in new trains.
"Given these factors, we have to view this report as a predominantly political document which has been released to coincide with the election campaign," said the company in a statement.
